fact_check.claim: 'now that we got the KCC20 protocol live, now we have Kaspa tokens, officially... the same way we say Solana tokens' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified: the KCC Coordination Forum declared KCC-1, KCC-2 and KCC-20 Final on October 21, 2026 (kcc20-live ledger, crypto.news); covenants have been live on mainnet since the Toccata upgrade on June 30, 2026; KRC-20 ownership was never enforced by Kaspa consensus (an off-chain indexer determined ownership) while KCC-20 puts token rules into scripts enforced by the network. The 'Kaspa tokens' naming is Mike's framing and is written as such. Copy: 'KCC-20 is final', 'rules live in covenants on the L1 itself', 'no third-party indexer deciding who owns what'.
fact_check.source: repurpose/output/kcc20-live-lane3-plan.json fact_check (crypto.news/kaspa-finalizes-kcc-native-token-app-standards/, news.bitcoin.com Kasplex indexer article); crypto.news re-surfaced 2026-10-28

fact_check.claim: 'Caspercom saying that they're doing something that's just going to move all the KRC-20s over to KCC-20... I saw a post from Nacho... they're going to do the migration soon' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified in the general form only: a KuCoin item reports KaspaCom building a one-way bridge to move KRC20 and Kaspa L2 tokens onto KCC-20, and Bitcoin.com (Sept 21) reports Nacho the Kat says the community intends to move to KCC-20; a kasplex GitHub comment (4 days old) describes NACHO's planned 'turnstile' migration tool. No official announcement that ALL KRC20s migrate, no launch date and no live bridge surfaced, so copy says 'KaspaCom is building a one-way bridge to move KRC20 tokens over to KCC-20' and 'Nacho the Kat already said it is moving', never 'all', 'soon' or 'live'. 'Caspercom' is the Whisper spelling of KaspaCom.

fact_check.claim: 'if Ghost Wallet is not updated... if Ghost Wallet is no longer maintained... better bet to have them in KasWare' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified as a maintenance signal, not as a shutdown: the ghost-wallet/web-extension GitHub repo shows its last update on December 30, 2024 (v0.0.190) and no 2026 release or discontinuation notice exists, so copy says 'Ghost Wallet's code on GitHub has not been updated since December 2024', never 'abandoned' or 'dead'. KasWare is a verified, maintained Kaspa browser-extension wallet (prior ledger). The 'Kaspa bot on Telegram' alternative Mike mentioned could not be identified and is not drafted. The 'people cannot get tokens out' line is kept as what people tell Mike, with his own tests working, exactly as he said it.
fact_check.source: github.com/ghost-wallet/web-extension/releases; github.com/ghost-wallet (Updated Dec 30, 2024); chromewebstore.google.com Ghost Wallet listing; kcc20-live ledger for KasWare (searched 2026-10-28)

fact_check.claim: 'The TAO token itself is not centralized... even like the founder stepped down out of the org' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified via consistent secondary reporting: in February 2026 co-founder Jacob Robert Steeves gave up the Opentensor Foundation CEO post and co-founder Ala Shaabana stepped aside from the COO role, framed as a response to centralization criticism; no primary OTF statement surfaced, so copy stays general: 'the founders stepped back from running the foundation in February'. fact_check.claim: 'near is proof of stake it has an infinite max supply... 2.5 percent inflation new tokens get put into circulation every year' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified: NEAR has no fixed max supply; nearcore 2.9.0 cut the maximum annual inflation rate from 5% to 2.5%, activated on mainnet on October 30, 2025 once 80% of block-producing validators adopted it; a further proposal to 1.6% is under discussion and is not drafted. Copy: 'Near is proof of stake with no max supply, and it only just cut its inflation cap from 5% to 2.5%'.
fact_check.source: blog.nearone.org/announcement/2025/10/21/enhancing-near-tokenomics.html; near.foundation blog (Oct 21, 2025); kucoin.com NEAR 1.6% proposal item (searched 2026-10-28)

yt_posts.topic: Kaspa tokens are official: what changed, the KRC20 migration path, wallet hygiene, 3.5 cents
yt_posts.body_style: news plus a two-item to-do list, with a first-person software-engineer read on migrations
yt_posts.body:
Kaspa tokens are official. The same way you say Solana tokens, ETH tokens or Sui tokens, you now say Kaspa tokens. And if you are holding KRC20 bags, there are two things to do before the migration, not after.

Start with what changed. A KRC20 balance was never enforced by Kaspa consensus. A third-party indexer read the chain and decided who owned what, and in September that indexer got tricked into crediting forged transfers and two token pools got drained. Kaspa itself was never touched. KCC-20, declared final on October 21, keeps the token rules in covenants on the Kaspa L1 itself; covenants have been live since Toccata on June 30. The network decides, not somebody's server. That is the whole reason this matters.

Now the migration. KaspaCom is building a one-way bridge to move KRC20 tokens over to KCC-20, and Nacho the Kat already said it is moving. So the old bags get a path. I am a software guy, and when you migrate a system between databases the entire job is making sure nobody loses anything. I would not expect anyone to build a token migration where holders lose tokens because of where they stored them. But better safe than sorry, which brings me to the second thing.

Check your wallet. Ghost Wallet's code on GitHub has not been updated since December 2024. People keep telling me they cannot get tokens out of it, and every time I go test it my own transfers in and out work fine. But a wallet that stopped shipping updates is not where I want my Kaspa tokens sitting through a standard change. If the software is not maintained, eventually the technology moves on without it. Move them to something that is actively maintained, KasWare for example, and do it before the bridge opens.

Price: $KAS is 3.5 cents while all of this ships, about 83% under its all-time high. If the whole market cracks and Bitcoin tags its 50-week SMA, Kaspa goes lower with it, maybe 3.2 cents, worst case something like 2.7. I DCA either way; a little here, a little there, and if it drops I have more to buy it with. Never financial advice.

So tell me in the comments: are you migrating your KRC20 bags on day one, or waiting to see who goes first? And name the wallet you are holding them in, because I want to know how many of you are still on Ghost.

Hit like and subscribe if you want the Kaspa updates explained before the rest of the market reads them.

yt_posts.topic: TAO is not competing with Near and Render, it is the arena; the centralization talk; the robotics narrative; price
yt_posts.body_style: hook-and-thesis-first argument: the arena, the centralization rebuttal, the narrative, the price
yt_posts.body:
Every week somebody tells me $TAO is competing against Near and Render. It is not. Bittensor is the arena they compete in, and the people calling it centralized keep buying things that are far more centralized. Let me walk through it.

Render is GPU compute. Near is more on the hosting side, with compute attached. On Bittensor, each of those is roughly one subnet's worth of work. Subnets compete for TAO emissions by producing the best output, and the arena pays the winners. One project does not have to beat the others; the whole point is that all of them line up inside the same incentive machine to produce the best decentralized AI. That is a different category of asset.

Now the centralization talk, because I hear it constantly. $TAO is hard capped at 21 million, the same number as Bitcoin, and this past February the founders stepped back from running the foundation. The network kept producing blocks like nothing happened. Yes, fewer people run nodes than eventually will; Bitcoin was the same in its early years. Compare it to what people buy without blinking: Near is proof of stake with no max supply at all, and it only just cut its annual inflation cap from 5% to 2.5%. Solana is more centralized than TAO. XRP is centralized and people buy it like crazy. I have made plenty of gains on tokens with worse tokenomics than this.

Then the narrative. BlackRock launched its first active robotics ETF on October 21, RBTX, with Tesla, AMD and Nvidia at the top of the book. Robots are about to be mass produced like cars, and the AI running inside them needs an inference layer nobody owns. That is the arena. And Anthropic filed for its IPO on October 26 with about $16.3 billion in revenue for the first half of 2026 versus $1.2 billion a year earlier. This is not 2000. The spending is massive and the revenue is showing up with it.

$TAO is about $258, roughly 66% under its $758 all-time high and down 17% on the month. I think you get many, many multipliers out of it from here, the same way I think it about Kaspa. Never financial advice.

So here is the question: if you had to hold one for five years, is it $TAO, $NEAR or $RENDER? And if you are in the TAO-is-centralized camp, give me the actual argument in the comments, because I want to answer it on stream.

Hit like and subscribe for the AI x crypto takes that ignore the four-year cycle echo chamber.
